header._comment: RAW frames captured from a live Zerodha WebSocket, recorded BEFORE any decode. Unlike fixtures.json these are ground truth from the venue, not constructed from the published layout. NO DECODED VALUES ARE STORED HERE, DELIBERATELY: a corpus that carries one implementation's reading hands that reading to every fixture derived from it, which re-closes the circle live capture exists to break. Expected values must be derived downstream by an oracle named with its version. STRUCTURE: a record is one WebSocket MESSAGE, not one packet. A message carries several packets and 'shapes' lists them, so the record count is NOT the packet count -- a deriver written against records will get the framing wrong.
header.sampling_limitation: kept=1 of 952 frames. This recorder shape-samples on (packet_len, segment) with a cap, and a SINGLE WebSocket message carried all four packets, taking that shape straight to its cap. So this corpus captures ONE INSTANT, and the question it was captured to answer -- whether exchange_timestamp and last_trade_time ever separate -- rested entirely on that first message happening to contain separated values. It did, and deep-OTM staleness made that likely, but LIKELY IS NOT DESIGNED: had it been coincident the run would have reported zero after five minutes of a market that opens only on weekdays. The sampler optimises LAYOUT coverage and this question needed TEMPORAL coverage. Fixed afterwards in capture_live_frames.py (MIN_SHAPE_INTERVAL_SECS spaces repeat samples of a shape in time); this corpus predates it.
header.coverage_limitation: Full mode only, four deep-OTM SENSEX strikes. Layouts 8/28/32/44 are ABSENT. This corpus is SUPPLEMENTARY to captured-2026-08-14-sensex-live.json, not a replacement, and nothing here should be read as whole-protocol coverage.
